title: Count Pairs That Form a Complete Day II
summary: Given an integer array representing times in hours, count the number of pairs i, j where i < j and the sum of hours[i] and hours[j] is an exact multiple of 24 hours.
statement: Given an integer array representing times in hours, count the number of pairs i, j where i < j and the sum of hours[i] and hours[j] is an exact multiple of 24 hours.
constraints: hours is a nonempty positive-integer array.
Count index pairs i<j whose sum is an exact multiple of 24.
Equal hour values at different indices count as distinct choices.
hints: Only each hour modulo 24 matters; a remainder r pairs with (-r) modulo 24.
Scan left to right, counting matching earlier complements before inserting the current remainder.
Every valid pair is counted exactly once when its later index is processed.
editorial: Every valid pair is counted exactly once when its later index is processed.

tests.explanation: The two twelves form one pair and the two multiples of 24 form another, totaling two.
Every pair sums to a multiple of 24, so all three pairs count.
